text:
Cutter Gauthier scored a hat trick, the last goal an empty-net-free snap with 34 seconds left that turned a two-goal game into a 5-2 win and stretched the Ducks' winning streak to five. Gauthier was the fifth pick in 2022 and went to Boston College before the NHL; on this night he finished with three goals and an assist, and Mikael Granlund had a goal and three assists beside him.

The scoreboard tells only part of it. Our numbers say Pittsburgh played the better game. The Penguins took 73 shot attempts to Anaheim's 58 and led in expected goals (a measure of chance quality) at even strength, 2.27 to 1.36. By our simulation of every shot, PIT deserved to win 73 percent of the time. The gap came from the goalies and the power play. Laurent Brossoit saved about 2.5 goals more than the chances against him called for, while Arturs Silovs gave back about one. The Ducks also scored on three of four power plays, including a Granlund snap on a 4 percent chance in the first period. Pittsburgh made it interesting late, with Kris Letang and Rickard Rakell scoring on the power play in the third to cut it to 4-2, and out-chanced Anaheim 1.97 to 0.89 in that period.

Anaheim leaves with five straight wins and a night where it needed every bit of its finishing. Pittsburgh gets a loss it can argue with, since the process held up even if the result did not. We'd watch whether the Penguins' pressure keeps producing chances, and whether Anaheim's goaltending and special teams can keep covering for a team that was outplayed.
